messages.subject: Random Sample
parts:
I have modified slightly the code that comes with Shiny to produce the following application:

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/carlosq/test2/

I want to use it to generate a random sample of students when I come to class. Those are the students that have to participate in class that particular day.

What I would like to do is :

Pick a sample size (say 5)
Hit the Update View Again
and Obtain a new random sample of 5.

The way it works now is :

I have to change the sample size and then press "Update View". If I don't change the value, the button does nothing.

Below I include both ui.R and server.R

ui.R

library(shiny)

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("Random Sample of Students"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select a dataset and specify the number
  # of observations to view
  sidebarPanel(
    numericInput("obs", "Number of observations to view:", 5),
    submitButton("Update View")
  ),

  # Show a summary of the dataset and an HTML table with the requested
  # number of observations
  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("view")
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Return the requested dataset
  datos <- read.csv("mba2014ni.csv",header=T)
 
  # Generate a summary of the dataset
 
  # Show the first "n" observations
  output$view <- renderTable({
    data.frame(estudiante=datos$estudiante[sample(1:73,size=input$obs,replace=TRUE)])
      })
})

messages.subject: Re: Random Sample
parts:
I think you want to use acionButton from shiny incubator with isolate(). See the example here:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/actionbutton/
Code here:
  https://gist.github.com/wch/4963887

The tutorial explains how it works -- but you might need to read the two previous sections under "Understanding Reactivity" for a full understanding of it:
  http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#isolation

-Winston
